judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line ratio whose two inputs are separately defined; nothing on its face to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the parallel 'Cash Sweep DSCR' (c030), built on different inputs, so the two ratios must be kept apart when applying Section 6.12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short account definition pointing to Section 5.15 and the Collateral Account Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02(d) (c217) forbids using loan proceeds to fund the DSRA while Section 2.06(j) (c231) directs cash collateral into the DSRA 'as supplemental to the Required Amount', a mild tension over what may be deposited there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any items treated as exceptional or extraordinary items' is an open-ended add-back with no stated standard beyond GAAP.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on 'Adjusted Net Income' (c012), which already excludes extraordinary items, so the add-back in (b) risks double-counting despite the 'without duplication' opener.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely mechanical trigger keyed to two condition-precedent sections.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.02(a)(i) (c214), which makes Tranche A-1 available once Sections 4.01 and 4.04 are satisfied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A label defined by reference to the Recitals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Recitals do identify EGL, so the reference works.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference, but it points to 'the Guarantee Agreement' in the singular when the instrument defines 'Guarantee Agreements' in the plural for two different guarantors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because c090 contemplates separate agreements for EGL (Exhibit E-1) and the Parent (Exhibit E-2), it is not clear which document supplies the release date, and the release of EGL is commercially significant to the Recitals' guarantee statement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or such other independent, professional and reputable engineering firm appointed' does not say who appoints or whose consent is needed, and the qualifiers are subjective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Commercial Operations Date definition (c038) and the Force Majeure Event definition (c084) both turn on this consultant's certificate or opinion, yet c038 calls it the 'Lenders' Engineering Consultant', an undefined variant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 9.14.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.14 is not reproduced; no conflict is visible in the available text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same open appointment formula as the Engineering Consultant, with no named firm and no stated appointing party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the 'Consultants' definition (c044) and Sections 4.02(k)/5.10(d), which are outside the reproduced text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'relating in any way to the environment' following a long enumeration of instrument types is about as broad a formulation as exists, and its outer boundary is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports 'Environmental Liability' (c061) and 'Hazardous Materials' (c093) coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (e) — any 'contract, agreement or other consensual arrangement pursuant to which liability is assumed' — is a catch-all appended to four specific heads.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Environmental Laws and Hazardous Materials definitions it depends on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition that expressly excludes the Borrower.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches 'EPC Contracts' (c063) and the named Essar-affiliate contracts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four named contracts followed by 'any other material contract entered into by the Borrower with respect to any engineering, procurement or construction services' — an unquantified 'material' catch-all against enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Project Contract' (c160) sweeps in every EPC Contract but then imposes a US$4,000,000 Contract Threshold on other contracts, so 'material' here and the Threshold there use different yardsticks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare naming definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in 'Supplier Financing' (c185) and 'Intercreditor Agreement' (c107).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard multi-entity equity definition including options and warrants.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'Equity Proceeds' (c066), 'Restricted Payment' (c170) and the LLC Pledge Agreement definition (c124).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A tight definition with a single express carve-out for employee equity sales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the mandatory prepayment events referenced in c103 and Section 2.11(c), which are not reproduced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently across the ERISA definitions, notwithstanding the OCR rendering 'BRISA'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise Code-referential test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'ERISA Event' (c069) and 'Plan' (c157).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed lettered list of statutory triggers with no residual catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with the ERISA definitions and Section 3.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires deposit of 'all Cash and receivables arising out of any contracts of the Borrower with any Person or payments otherwise received by Borrower' — a sweep so total that it is hard to give a workable boundary, and the stated purpose ('to be applied in accordance with the Cash Sweep Mechanism') does not match a general receipts account.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.05 (c223) directs all loan proceeds into the same Escrow Account for disbursement to the Borrower for Project costs, and c103 directs insurance, equity and asset-sale proceeds into a separate Insurance and Other Proceeds Account, so three provisions claim overlapping receipts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The successor limb refers to 'any successor collateral agent', a role this Agreement does not define, the defined roles being Security Agent and Escrow Agent and Account Bank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Security Agent' (c176) is the separately defined collateral holder, so the stray reference could be read to blur the two agency roles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'refers to whether such Loan, or the Loans comprising such Borrowing, are bearing interest at a rate determined by reference to the LIBO Rate' is grammatically defective — a definition cannot sensibly 'refer to whether' something is true.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.03(c) (c220) says every Borrowing 'shall be comprised entirely of Eurodollar Rate Borrowings', which is itself circular given this definition, and Section 2.14 contemplates a non-LIBO alternative that the definition does not accommodate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical Regulation D definition with an automatic-adjustment sentence; specific and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the interest and increased-costs provisions without visible conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Article VII.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VII is not reproduced, but Sections 2.06(j) and 2.07(d) invoke it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long six-limb exclusion with nested exceptions, but each limb is drafted with tax-specific precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with 'Indemnified Taxes' (c097), 'Other Taxes' (c145) and Sections 2.17 and 2.19, which are not reproduced; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative verb is missing — '"Existing Credit Agreement" the Credit Agreement dated September 22, 2010' — so on its face the definition does not define anything.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term is used in the conditions precedent and negative covenants that are not reproduced; nothing in the available text conflicts with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure back-reference to the Recitals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Recitals do define 'Facilities' as the Term Loan Facility plus the Letter of Credit Facility, so the reference works, though it makes a recital operative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A naming definition with a successor limb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'Agents' (c015) and the preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numerator's parenthetical gloss on fixed assets ('tangible assets not expected to be converted to cash within the current fiscal year') is an ad hoc test, and the denominator strings together several classes of debt with a pari passu qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its gloss on fixed assets uses a 'current fiscal year' horizon while 'Current Assets' (c046) uses a rolling one-year horizon, so an asset can fall into both or neither.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to a definition embedded in another definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Excluded Taxes definition (c075) does introduce 'FATCA', so the pointer works.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes two numerical conditions, so the wording itself is definite, though it describes an event that is entirely outside the Borrower's control.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires Total Commitments of US$530,000,000 when the operative 'Total Commitment' (c199) is US$250,000,000 unless accessions occur, and it requires Supplier Financing of US$182,750,000 while 'Supplier Financing' (c185) is capped at US$183,000,000; since Tranche B (c215) is available only after Financial Closure, this is the sort of gateway two parties would read very differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare cross-reference to Section 6.12.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Relevant Date' (c165) refers to 'the financial Covenants' in lower case, a stylistic mismatch only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of four offices with no catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside 'Responsible Officer' (c169), a broader list, and the two are used for different certifications without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumeration of specific events closing with 'or other similar acts beyond the reasonable control of the Borrower' — the paradigm general-versus-specific problem, compounded by the 90-day delay gate and dependence on the Engineering Consultant's opinion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its trigger is measured from the 'Scheduled Commercial Operations Date' (c172), a date the parties must still agree at Financial Closure, so the force majeure test cannot be applied until that date is fixed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence ('If a Borrower is located in more than one jurisdiction') is leftover multi-borrower form language, and 'located' is left undefined for a Minnesota LLC.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is only one Borrower under c020, so the sentence has no application, and the same plural residue appears in 'Obligor' (c143) and Section 2.06(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line accounting-standards definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.03 (c212) layers IFRS on top for the Guarantors and provides a GAAP-change freeze mechanism, which coexists with rather than contradicts this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but conventional formulation with an express supranational-body inclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the tax, environmental and approvals definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific dated contract by contract number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties to 'Great Lakes Litigation' (c089) and to the litigation-related carve-outs in c012, c013 and c198, which are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'and related proceedings thereto that may be filed elsewhere in Federal or state court' is an open-ended extension whose reach ('related') is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several definitions (c012(7), c013(m), c198) turn on an action 'that would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect' rather than on this defined litigation, so the two ways of describing the same dispute could diverge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short form-referential definition naming two exhibits for two guarantors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c056 refers to 'the Guarantee Agreement' in the singular for the EGL Guarantee Release Date, and the Recitals describe the guarantee in general terms, so which agreement governs release is not squarely resolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'either of (i) the Parent or (ii) EGL, as the case may be' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Recitals, c090 and 'Obligor' (c143).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional four-limb guaranty definition with an express endorsement carve-out; broad but standard and internally structured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is folded into 'Indebtedness' (c096) clause (f), which adds its own catch-all for 'any obligation undertaken ... in the nature of a payment obligation', partially overlapping.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list closing with 'all other hazardous or toxic substances or wastes of any nature regulated pursuant to any Environmental Law', a catch-all bounded only by the equally broad Environmental Laws definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c060 and c061.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or other derivative transaction of any kind or nature' is an unbounded catch-all following four specific hedge types.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Indebtedness' (c096)(k) sweeps in all Hedging Agreement obligations while 'Net Debt' (c138) backs out small mark-to-market amounts under Permitted Hedging Agreements, so the treatment of hedges varies across the financial definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard accounting-standards definition with two inclusive limbs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.03 (c212) applies IFRS to the Guarantors and GAAP to the Borrower, which is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eleven-limb list containing genuinely open catch-alls — notably 'any put options, shortfall undertakings, letters of comfort or any obligation undertaken by such Person in the nature of a payment obligation' — plus a final attribution sentence for partnership-type liability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge for 'Long-Term Debt' (c127), 'Short-Term Debt' (c179), 'Net Debt' (c138) and Section 6.01, each of which re-cuts the same categories with its own inclusions and exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line residual definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on c075 and c145, which are drafted to be mutually exclusive.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A naming definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble, 'Lender' (c117) and 'Issuing Bank' (c113).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cross-reference to Section 2.02(a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02(a) (c214) subdivides Tranche A into A-1 and A-2 without contradicting this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed dollar figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: US$150,000,000 plus the Tranche B figure of US$100,000,000 equals the US$250,000,000 Total Commitment (c199), which is coherent.
